thread_title: S. alata (various clones) St. Tammany Parish, LA
breadcrumb: S. alata (various clones) St. Tammany Parish, LA

posts.body_html:
Now I know a bunch of you are thinking, "man, I don't remember Sarracenia naturally occurring in LA" and you're right, they don't occur in Los Angeles or Los Altos, but they do occur in Louisiana, buda-boom-CH!

Interestingly enough, despite torrential rains this season, as well as countless freezes, some of the traps are still looking well in March! If you're looking to breed plants that have traps with longevity/evergreen traits, maybe these genetics are something to consider. Pics taken 3/28/25:







some atrorubras up in this mix!
